title: Words Hidden Inside Other Words
statement:
You get a list of distinct lowercase words words. Return every word that appears as a contiguous substring of at least one other word in the list.

Each such word is listed once, even if it hides inside several words. The answer may be in any order.

examples.why: Both are inside "seat". "tea" uses the same letters, but they are not contiguous in that order anywhere.
"de" is inside both "code" and "decode", but it is reported once.
Sharing letters is not enough; none contains another.

constraints: words[i] contains only lowercase English letters
hints: With at most 100 short words, comparing every pair is affordable.
For each word, ask: is it a substring of some other word? Stop at the first one found so it is added once.
A shortcut: join all words with a separator that cannot appear in a word. A word hidden in another word then occurs at least twice in the joined string.

explain.intuition:
The sizes are tiny: 100 words of at most 30 letters. Checking every word against every other word with a built-in substring search costs about 100 · 100 · 30 · 30 character comparisons in the worst case, which is fast. The care goes into the details: skip comparing a word with itself, and break after the first match so each word is reported once.

A neat alternative joins all words with a space. Every word occurs once as itself; if it is also inside another word, it occurs again. Comparing indexOf with lastIndexOf detects the second occurrence. Since words are distinct, the extra occurrence can only come from inside a longer word.
steps: Look through every other word at index j ≠ i.
If that word contains w, add w to the answer and stop looking for it.
pitfalls: Comparing a word with itself, which marks every word as hidden.
Adding a word once per containing word, so "de" appears twice.
Checking for shared letters or a subsequence instead of a contiguous substring.

complexity.time: O(n² · L²) with naive substring search

solutions.title: Check every pair
solutions.idea: For each word, search for it inside every other word; stop at the first hit.

solutions.title: Search one joined string
solutions.idea: Join all words with a space. A word found at two different places must also live inside another word.

followups: There are 100 000 words. Which structure finds every word that occurs inside another faster than pairwise checks?
Return, for each hidden word, the shortest word that contains it.
